extracted.intended_audience: Users of GAP (computational group theorists, mathematicians and programmers who use GAP)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for GAP functions that construct classical and projective groups, query conjugacy classes, and access group libraries (perfect groups, integral matrix groups), including parameter semantics, defaults, and displayed invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: SpecialOrthogonalGroup constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: constructs a group isomorphic to the special orthogonal group SO(e,d,q), the subgroup of GO(e,d,q) with determinant one, in the category given by the filter filt. (The index of SO(e,d,q) in GO(e,d,q) is 2 if q is odd, and 1 if q is even.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filt is not given it defaults to IsMatrixGroup (44.1.1), and the returned group is the special orthogonal group itself. If Forms package version ≥ 1.2.6 is loaded then the quadratic form can be specified via form, which may be a matrix or a form object in IsQuadraticForm or a group with stored InvariantQuadraticForm (and then this form is taken). A given form determines e and d, and also q except if form is a matrix that does not store its BaseDomain value. These parameters can be entered, and an error is signalled if they do not fit to the given form. If form is not given then a default is chosen as described in the introduction to Section 50.2. Examples: SpecialOrthogonalGroup(5,3) -> SO(0,5,3); SpecialOrthogonalGroup(IsPermGroup,5,3) -> Perm_SO(0,5,3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Omega constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: constructs a group isomorphic to Ω(e,d,q) of d×d matrices over GF(q) that respect a non-singular quadratic form specified by e and that have square spinor norm in odd characteristic or Dickson invariant 0 in even characteristic, in the category given by filt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For odd q and d≥2 this group has index two in the corresponding SO(e,d,q). The value of e must be 0 for odd d (and can optionally be omitted), and one of 1 or −1 for even d. If filt omitted defaults to IsMatrixGroup. If Forms package version ≥1.2.6 is loaded desired quadratic form may be specified via form (matrix, form object, or group with InvariantQuadraticForm). A given form determines e,d and q except if form matrix lacks BaseDomain; an error is signalled if parameters do not fit. If form omitted a default is chosen. Examples show StructureDescription outputs for specific Omega calls and illustrate that different forms may give non-subset relations (IsSubset example).

rubrics_metrics.name: GeneralSemilinearGroup constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: GeneralSemilinearGroup returns a group isomorphic to the general semilinear group ΓL(d,q) of semilinear mappings of the vector space GF(q)^d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filt is not given it defaults to IsMatrixGroup (44.1.1). The returned group consists of matrices of dimension d*f over the field with p elements, where q = p^f for a prime p. (Provides the relationship between q and the base field used.)

rubrics_metrics.name: SpecialSemilinearGroup constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: SpecialSemilinearGroup returns a group isomorphic to the special semilinear group ΣL(d,q) of those semilinear mappings of GF(q)^d whose linear part has determinant one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filt is not given it defaults to IsMatrixGroup (44.1.1), and the returned group consists of matrices of dimension d*f over the field with p elements, where q = p^f for a prime integer p.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProjectiveGeneralLinearGroup constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: constructs a group isomorphic to the projective general linear group PGL(d,q) of d×d matrices over GF(q), modulo the centre, in the category given by filt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filt is not given it defaults to IsPermGroup (43.1.1), and the returned group is the action on lines of the underlying vector space (i.e., natural permutation action on 1-dimensional subspaces).

rubrics_metrics.name: ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: constructs a group isomorphic to the projective special linear group PSL(d,q) of d×d matrices over GF(q) whose determinant is the identity, modulo the centre, in the category given by filt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filt is not given it defaults to IsPermGroup (43.1.1), and the returned group is the action on lines of the underlying vector space.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProjectiveGeneralUnitaryGroup constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: constructs a group isomorphic to the projective general unitary group PGU(d,q) of d×d matrices over GF(q^2) that respect a fixed nondegenerate sesquilinear form, modulo the centre, in the category given by filt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filt omitted it defaults to IsPermGroup and the returned group is the action on lines of the underlying vector space. The constructor expects matrices preserving a chosen sesquilinear form over GF(q^2).

rubrics_metrics.name: ProjectiveSpecialUnitaryGroup constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: constructs a group isomorphic to the projective special unitary group PSU(d,q) of d×d matrices over GF(q^2) that respect a fixed nondegenerate sesquilinear form and have determinant 1, modulo the centre, in the category given by filt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filt omitted default IsPermGroup; returned group is action on lines. Use when you need determinant-1 unitary projective group.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProjectiveSymplecticGroup constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: constructs a group isomorphic to the projective symplectic group PSp(d,q) of d×d matrices over GF(q) that respect a fixed nondegenerate symplectic form, modulo the centre, in the category given by filt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filt not given defaults to IsPermGroup and returned group is the action on lines of the underlying vector space. (Also synonyms PSP and PSp provided.)

rubrics_metrics.name: ProjectiveGeneralOrthogonalGroup constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: constructs a group isomorphic to the projective group PGO(e,d,q) of GO(e,d,q), modulo the centre, in the category given by filt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filt omitted defaults to IsPermGroup and the returned group is the action on lines of the underlying vector space. Use e and d parameters per GeneralOrthogonalGroup conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProjectiveSpecialOrthogonalGroup constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: constructs a group isomorphic to the projective group PSO(e,d,q) of SO(e,d,q), modulo the centre, in the category given by filt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filt omitted defaults to IsPermGroup and the returned group is the action on lines of the underlying vector space.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProjectiveOmega constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: constructs a group isomorphic to the projective group PΩ(e,d,q) of Ω(e,d,q), modulo the centre, in the category given by filt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filt omitted defaults to IsPermGroup and the returned group is the action on lines of the underlying vector space.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProjectiveGeneralSemilinearGroup constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: ProjectiveGeneralSemilinearGroup returns a group isomorphic to the factor group of the general semilinear group ΓL(d,q) modulo the center of its normal subgroup GL(d,q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filt omitted defaults to IsPermGroup and the returned group is the action on lines of the underlying vector space GF(q)^d. Use when projectivizing ΓL by the central scalars in GL(d,q).

rubrics_metrics.name: ProjectiveSpecialSemilinearGroup constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: ProjectiveSpecialSemilinearGroup returns a group isomorphic to the factor group of the special semilinear group ΣL(d,q) modulo the center of its normal subgroup SL(d,q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filt omitted defaults to IsPermGroup and the returned group is the action on lines of GF(q)^d.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugacy classes in classical groups note
rubrics_metrics.description: For general and special linear groups GAP has an efficient method to generate representatives of the conjugacy classes using results from linear algebra on normal forms of matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method is efficient for GL/SL types; the manual invites users to provide methods for other classical groups if they know how to do this. Example: computing NrConjugacyClasses and ConjugacyClasses for SL(4,9).

rubrics_metrics.name: NrConjugacyClassesGL family functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions NrConjugacyClassesGL, NrConjugacyClassesGU, NrConjugacyClassesSL, NrConjugacyClassesSU, NrConjugacyClassesPGL, NrConjugacyClassesPGU, NrConjugacyClassesPSL, NrConjugacyClassesPSU, NrConjugacyClassesSLIsogeneous, NrConjugacyClassesSUIsogeneous compute the number of conjugacy classes for the listed classical groups for given n and prime power q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For isogeneous groups (divisors f of n), NrConjugacyClassesSLIsogeneous computes number for the corresponding group; extreme cases f=1 and f=n give SL(n,q) and PGL(n,q). Formulae for the counts are taken from Mac81. Examples show very large outputs for high parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructor naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: All functions described in the previous sections call constructor operations whose names are obtained from the function names by appending "Cons" (e.g., CyclicGroup calls CyclicGroupCons(cat,n)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first argument cat for each method of such a constructor must be the category for which the method is installed. Example of InstallMethod usage is provided, showing the required signature and filters.

rubrics_metrics.name: InstallMethod usage note
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for constructors are installed with InstallMethod and require a category string and type specifications for arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows InstallMethod(CyclicGroupCons, "regular perm group", true, [IsPermGroup and IsRegularProp and IsFinite, IsInt and IsPosRat], 0, function(filter,n) ... end ); indicating how to register constructor methods for categories and argument types.

rubrics_metrics.name: AllLibraryGroups selection function semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: AllLibraryGroups-style functions let you select all groups from a library that have a given set of properties using pairs (function, value_or_list).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each pair: the first argument is a function applied to library groups, the second is a single value or list of acceptable values. For AllSmallGroups the first function must be Size and it supports alternative syntax omitting Size. The selection functions are implemented efficiently by recognizing a set of precomputed properties for the library. Examples: AllTransitiveGroups(NrMovedPoints,[10..15], Size,[1..100], IsAbelian, false) returns transitive groups with degree between 10 and 15, size <100, and not abelian. Implementation pseudocode shows membership checks and list support.

rubrics_metrics.name: OneLibraryGroup family semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: For each AllLibraryGroups function there is a corresponding OneLibraryGroup function (OneSmallGroup, OneIrreducibleSolvableGroup, OneTransitiveGroup, OnePrimitiveGroup) that returns at most one group with the prescribed properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OneLibraryGroup functions accept exactly the same arguments as the AllLibraryGroups variant and return a single matching group or fail if none exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfect groups library scope and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The GAP library of finite perfect groups provides, up to isomorphism, a list of all perfect groups whose sizes are less than 2·10^6, incorporating work of Holt and Plesken and later additions and corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some orders were only counted in the original work (not listed); additional groups found by contributors are included. The manual recommends Holt and Plesken's book for further information and credits contributors who converted data to GAP format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and computation note for perfect groups
rubrics_metrics.description: All groups are stored by presentations, and permutation representations are obtained by coset enumeration; some library groups may not have a faithful permutation representation of small degree and computations may be time consuming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should be aware of potential performance issues when working with certain stored perfect groups; the library stores presentations and subgroup lists that yield permutation representations by coset action.

rubrics_metrics.name: SizesPerfectGroups() behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: SizesPerfectGroups() returns the ordered list of all numbers up to 2·10^6 that occur as sizes of perfect groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One can iterate over parts of the perfect groups library using SizesPerfectGroups together with NrPerfectGroups and PerfectGroup to access groups of those sizes; example loops provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: PerfectGroup constructor semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: PerfectGroup([filt,] size[, n]) or PerfectGroup([filt,] size_numberpair) returns a group isomorphic to the library group specified by size and index n (default n=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional filt defines the filter in which the group is returned; possible filters: IsPermGroup and IsSubgroupFpGroup. In the IsSubgroupFpGroup case generators and relators coincide with those in [HP89]. The default filter is IsPermGroup. Examples demonstrate obtaining groups and checking NrMovedPoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: PerfectIdentification attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: PerfectIdentification(G) attribute is set for all groups obtained from the perfect groups library and has the value [size,n] if the group is obtained with these parameters from the library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this attribute to identify which library entry produced a group.

rubrics_metrics.name: NumberPerfectGroups and historical variants behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: NumberPerfectGroups(size) (synonym NrPerfectGroups) returns the number of non-isomorphic perfect groups of order size for size ≤ 2·10^6; NumberPerfectLibraryGroups (and NrPerfectLibraryGroups) exist for historical reasons and return 0 instead of fail for arguments outside the library scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For odd size an answer is returned and odd order groups are solvable. For out-of-range arguments NumberPerfectGroups returns fail; the library variant returns 0 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: SizeNumbersPerfectGroups semantics and accepted inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: SizeNumbersPerfectGroups(factor1,factor2,...) returns a list of pairs (group order, number of library groups) that contain the specified factors among their composition factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each argument must be either the name of a nonabelian simple group (from an accepted list of string forms) or an integer (product of sizes of cyclic factors). The function replaces all integer arguments by their product. The manual lists accepted simple-group name forms (e.g., An, Ln(q), Un(q), Sp4(4), Sz(8), Mn, Jn) with allowed ranges and notes on naming restrictions (names compared as text strings). Note: in this library PSU(n,q) denotes the factor group of SU(n,q) by its centre as defined here.

rubrics_metrics.name: DisplayInformationPerfectGroups output items
rubrics_metrics.description: DisplayInformationPerfectGroups(size[,n]) displays invariants of the n-th group of order size from the perfect groups library (or all groups of that size if n omitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information displayed includes: a headline containing size number [size,n], a message if G is simple or quasisimple, the "description" of G as in Holt-Plesken [HP89], size of the centre (suppressed if simple), prime decomposition of |G|, orbit sizes for a faithful permutation representation provided by the library, and references to occurrences of G in HP89 (class numbers and internal numbers). Examples show formatting and multiple group outputs. Alternative input [size,n] may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of orbit size(s) in DisplayInformationPerfectGroups
rubrics_metrics.description: The displayed 'orbit size = k' indicates an available transitive permutation representation of degree k; 'orbit sizes = a + b' indicates a nontransitive permutation representation acting on two orbits of sizes a and b, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DisplayInformationPerfectGroups shows the available permutation representation degrees; users can construct these representations via the subgroup lists provided in the library (coset action on listed subgroups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for group descriptions from HP89 (composition factor notation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The "description" notation used in the library (from HP89) lists composition factors from the top of the group downwards and uses additional symbols to indicate relations and extension types between factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols: '×' = direct product; 'C' (commutator) between factors means the second lies in the commutator subgroup of the first; 'A' (abelian) indicates the second is in the pth power (but not commutator) of the first; 'E' (elementary abelian) indicates together they generate elementary abelian group (modulo later factors) but extension does not split; 'N' (nonsplit) before a factor indicates splitting properties. Examples and caveats (notation can be imprecise) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imf library scope and definitions (irreducible maximal finite integral matrix groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: The library contains Q-class representatives for irreducible maximal finite integral matrix groups of dimension ≤31 and Z-class representatives for dimensions ≤11 or for dimensions 13,17,19,23; deals with Z-classes (conjugacy under GL_n(Z)) and Q-classes (conjugacy under GL_n(Q)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two types of i.m.f. subgroups distinguished: those maximal finite in GL_n(Q) (Q1(n)) and those not (Q2(n)). For groups in Q2(n) there is a uniquely determined rational i.m.f. class C ∈ Q1(n) such that the group is conjugate under Q to a proper subgroup of some H∈C. The library provides integral representatives for all Q1(n) and, for certain dimensions, for Q2(n) and Z-classes. Each group stored with matrix generators and Gram matrix of associated positive definite symmetric form; short vectors and their orbits are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: ImfNumberQQClasses / ImfNumberQClasses / ImfNumberZClasses semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: ImfNumberQQClasses(dim) returns q1(dim) (number of Q-classes of i.m.f. rational matrix groups of dimension dim). ImfNumberQClasses(dim) returns number of Q-classes available in the library for dimension dim. ImfNumberZClasses(dim,q) returns number of Z-classes in the q-th Q-class for dimension dim (when known).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valid dim values up to 31 for Q-classes; when Z-classes known (dim ≤11 or dim ∈ {13,17,19,23}) the list of Q-classes is arranged so Q1(dim) classes precede Q2(dim). ImfNumberQClasses equals q1+q2 when Z-classes are known, else equals q1. ImfNumberZClasses only valid when Z-classes known for given dim.

rubrics_metrics.name: DisplayImfInvariants output and parameter behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: DisplayImfInvariants(dim,q[,z]) displays Z-class invariants for the z-th Z-class in the q-th Q-class of i.m.f. integral matrix groups of dimension dim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed items: Z-class number (dim.q.z) if dim ≤11 or prime ≤23, else Q-class number (dim.q); a message if group is solvable; size; isomorphism type; elementary divisors of associated quadratic form; sizes of orbits of short vectors (degrees of faithful permutation representations); norm of associated short vectors; and if group is not i.m.f. in GL_n(Q) an appropriate message including Q-class number of corresponding rational i.m.f. class. If parameter dim,q,or z is 0 the command loops over all available values. z default is 1; z≠1 must not be specified if Z-classes are not known for given dim. Greatest legal dim is 31. Examples show formatting (solvable message, isomorphism type, elementary divisors, orbit sizes, minimal norm).
